title: unified-rollouts: weighted canary + shadow AB autorollback with stability guards
author: Priya Nair
description: Motivation: Improve rollout safety and flexibility by combining weighted canary, shadow A/B traffic, and an automated rollback workflow with explicit stability guards. Production incidents in the last quarter showed gaps when transient metric spikes or noisy signals caused premature rollbacks or allowed regression to slip through shadow traffic. This PR introduces: 1) a weighted canary controller that supports fractional traffic shifts and stable hold windows; 2) shadow A/B plumbing to run candidate and baseline models in parallel with separate metric buckets; 3) a multi-metric autorollback engine that evaluates composite signals (latency p99, error-rate, model-quality regression from eval harness) and applies stability guards (minimum sample size, hysteresis windows, and sustained violation thresholds); 4) e2e and unit tests, observability hooks, and docs updates. Implementation summary: - New controller: rollout/weighted_canary_controller.go — handles targetTraffic splits, hold windows, and ramp steps. - Shadow router: routing/shadow_ab.go — duplicates requests to shadow candidate and baseline routes and tags metrics. - Autorollback policy engine: rollout/autorollback_engine.go — configurable policy predicates, multi-metric matching, and automatic rollback actions with safe-fallbacks. - Stability guards: rollout/stability_guards.go — enforces minSampleSize, gracePeriod, and sliding-window aggregation to prevent reacting to noise. - Metrics and traces: observability/rollout_metrics.go + tracing points in controller paths. - Tests: e2e/rollout_shadow_canary_test.go (adds a simulated traffic harness), unit tests for policy evaluation, and integration tests that run against the canary simulator. Backwards compatibility: All new features are opt-in via Rollout spec fields (weightedCanary, shadowAB, autorollbackPolicy). Existing Rollout CRs without these fields behave as before. Migration notes: default behavior is unchanged; the new weighted canary scheduler will only take effect when a rollout declares weightedCanary: true. Security and privacy: shadow A/B duplicates request payloads but enforces tenant data filters and respects redaction policies; there is opt-out in rollout spec for payload duplication. Related: references ENG-4821 (design doc), ENG-4900 (observability work), SUP-987 (customer incident).

review_comments: Ethan Park: overall looks good — two high level asks: (1) make minSampleSize configurable per metric, (2) add a fallback that pins to last-known-good model when rollout controller loses leader election.
Priya Nair: replied — added minSampleSize as part of AutorollbackPolicy and implemented leader-election fallback that pins to previous stable revision. See commit d4e5f6a.

Maya Singh: requested that we surface detailed rollback rationale in the rollout event stream (which we can link to on Console). Also asked for clearer e2e scenarios reproducing intermittent p99 spikes.
Priya Nair: replied — added detailed event payloads in rollout events and extended e2e test to include synthetic p99 spikes and transient errors.
Luca Rossi: nit — prefer consistent naming of "holdWindow" vs "hold_window" in YAML. Suggested schema comment. Priya accepted and normalized to snake_case for CRD fields.
Ethan Park: approval after CI fixes. \n(checked behavior in staging with a simulated 10k requests run; autorollback triggered correctly on sustained quality regression and respected stability guards)
release_notes:
- Added weighted canary rollout controller with fractional traffic steps and hold windows.
- Added shadow A/B routing to evaluate candidate vs baseline in parallel without impacting production traffic.
- Introduced multi-metric autorollback policies with stability guards (minSampleSize, hysteresis windows, sustained-violation thresholds).
- Added e2e simulator tests and observability hooks for rollback rationale and per-revision metrics.
